Case Name: Health endpoint exposes readiness state for automated probing
Precondition:
1. registry-center is deployed via docker compose
2. The health probe endpoint path is known (e.g. /health)
Steps:
1. GET /health to call the health probe endpoint see result 1
2. Parse the readiness state field in the response body see result 2
3. Cleanup: probing is read-only; confirm no leftover test data
Expected Result:
1. The health endpoint returns 200
2. The readiness state field value is recognizable by external automation (e.g. ready=true)
3. No leftover test data

Case Name: Failed registration emits ERROR log with error code and context
Precondition:
1. registry-center is deployed and service logs are readable via docker compose logs
2. An invalid AgentCard payload with missing required fields has been constructed
Steps:
1. POST /v1/agents with the invalid payload to trigger a registration failure
2. Search docker compose logs for the server-side log of that request see result 1
3. Inspect the service error count / status metric output see result 2
4. Cleanup: delete any leftover test data produced by this trigger (if any)
Expected Result:
1. A corresponding ERROR-level record appears in the service log, containing the error reason, Agent name, and request context
2. The error count / metric increments accordingly; no silent failure
3. No leftover test data

Case Name: Externalized service config survives compose recreate
Precondition:
1. registry-center is deployed via docker compose with the config file externally mounted
2. One test Agent has been registered
Steps:
1. Modify the log-level setting in the externalized config file see result 1
2. docker compose up -d --force-recreate to recreate the container
3. Query the Agent registered before the recreate and check the service state see result 2
4. Cleanup: delete the test-registered Agent
Expected Result:
1. The externalized config takes effect; recreating the container does not require rebuilding the image
2. After the recreate the service runs normally and the previously registered Agent data is retained without loss
3. After cleanup, the query returns 404

Case Name: Service self-heals after registry-center container stop
Precondition:
1. registry-center is deployed with at least 1 Agent registered
2. A docker compose environment is available
Steps:
1. Record the current list of registered Agents
2. docker compose stop registry-center to stop the container
3. Observe the container's automatic restart and service recovery see result 1
4. Query the Agent registered before the stop see result 2
5. Cleanup: delete the test-registered Agent data
Expected Result:
1. The container is automatically brought up by the compose restart policy and the service recovers
2. The previously registered Agent is still retrievable with no data loss, and other services in the same environment are unaffected
3. After cleanup, the query returns 404

Case Name: Bulk registration of 100 agents completes within 30 seconds
Precondition:
1. registry-center is deployed and docker stats is available
2. A test Agent name prefix has been agreed (perf-agent-)
Steps:
1. Register 100 Agents in a loop and record the total elapsed time see result 1
2. Observe container CPU and memory usage during registration see result 2
3. Query with pagination to confirm the total registered count see result 3
4. Cleanup: batch-delete the 100 test Agents and confirm the count returns to zero
Expected Result:
1. Total elapsed time for registering 100 Agents does not exceed 30 seconds
2. During registration there is no continuously rising memory, no OOM, and no request backlog errors
3. The queried total is 100 and all are retrievable
4. After cleanup, the Agent total returns to the pre-registration baseline

Case Name: Registration without valid auth token is rejected and audited
Precondition:
1. registry-center is deployed with authentication mode enabled
2. A valid test token and an invalid token have been prepared
Steps:
1. POST /v1/agents without the Authorization header see result 1
2. Call the registration API again with the invalid token see result 2
3. Search the audit logs related to the authentication failures see result 3
4. Cleanup: confirm no Agent was created and delete leftover test data (if any)
Expected Result:
1. Returns 401/403; no Agent is created
2. The invalid-token request is blocked and no business logic is executed
3. The authentication failures are recorded in audit logs
4. No leftover test data

Case Name: Registration payload with unknown extra fields stays backward compatible
Precondition:
1. The current version of registry-center is deployed
2. A valid AgentCard payload has been prepared
Steps:
1. POST /v1/agents with a valid payload plus unknown extension fields see result 1
2. GET /v1/agents/{name} to query that Agent and verify the known fields see result 2
3. Cleanup: delete the Agent registered in this case
Expected Result:
1. Returns 201; the unknown extension fields do not affect registration success (backward compatible)
2. The known fields returned by the query match the submitted content
3. After cleanup, the query returns 404
